_README: Fitted on ALL labelled data for deployment. NOT for scoring: every number in results/ comes from cross-validated fits that never saw the onion they scored.

defect._note: agmark_cuts are the statutory 1/5 and 1/2 and are never fitted

anomaly._note: fitted on healthy onions only; threshold is the 95th percentile of HEALTHY pixel distances

scale._note: SAM mask area scales as resolution^1.525, not ^2 (Phase 11)

detector._note: coin rule removed 54/72 spurious boxes and 0/537 onions

reported_performance._note: cross-validated, grouped by physical onion; see results/phase12

domain_guard._note: Photograph-level out-of-domain guard, two independent directions. A: the anomaly score says everything looks strange -- across the 53 calibration photographs the per-photo MEDIAN anomaly never exceeded 0.287 and the flagged fraction never exceeded 0.333. B: the defect rule says nothing registers at all -- the per-photo MAXIMUM raw defect fraction never fell below 0.0985 and no onion ever read exactly zero. Both cuts sit outside the observed range, so the guard fires on 0 of 53 in-domain photographs. B exists because a brightening shift drives every raw fraction to 0.0 while the anomaly score goes DOWN, not up: direction A is blind to it. See results/phase16b.

onion_gate._note: Per-detection 'is this an onion?' check, run before grading. p(not onion) >= reject_at: box dropped. review_at <= p < reject_at: kept but flagged for a human. If more than photo_reject_fraction of detections are dropped (or none survive), the whole photo is refused. Measured on 50 tray photos / 438 non-coin detections: no real onion reached 0.8 (highest 0.55); the 2 detections above 0.8 were bare floor. The web-page screenshot's 4 detections (faces, lamp) scored 0.978-0.995. Re-measure with: python -m onion_grader.gatecheck
onion_gate._faces_note: Boxes covering a human face (OpenCV YuNet, face_yunet.onnx) are dropped. The onion classifier alone missed a vendor's face in a market photo (called it 12% not-onion). Real faces scored 0.88-0.92; on the 50 tray photos YuNet's false 'faces' never exceeded 0.86, so >=0.9 is trusted outright and 0.8-0.9 only when the classifier also calls the face crop not-onion (tray false faces never above 0.26). A box is dropped when >=50% of the face lies inside it and the face is >=20% of the box.
onion_gate._context_note: Each box is also scored widened by context_pad on every side; rejection uses the higher not-onion score. A tight box on a toenail scored 0.33-0.77 (kept as an onion), with the foot in view 0.83-0.94. On 575 real onions the widened view never exceeded 0.65. 0 turns it off.

verdict._note: HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY comes from the v5 classifier (onion_gate_v5.pth). 5-fold cross-validation split by photo on the 538 hand-labelled tray onions: 98.3% balanced (193/198 rotten caught, 337/340 sound passed) vs 88.5% for the old v3 model (onion_gate.pth) with its threshold tuned the same way. Results are flat for any threshold 0.2-0.8, so 0.5 is used and 0.3-0.7 is reported as BORDERLINE. The AGMARK band is kept consistent: unhealthy -> at least Class I; p<0.2 -> Extra Class; otherwise the area band with a review flag. To go back to v3: weights 'onion_gate.pth', unhealthy_at 0.5.
verdict._borderline_note: p_unhealthy in [0.3, 0.7) -> verdict BORDERLINE (check by hand), not counted as healthy or unhealthy. On the 538 hand-labelled tray onions (cross-validated) 0 fell in this range, and v5 was equally accurate at any threshold 0.2-0.8. On new photos (vivo Y29, concrete floor, 2026-09-22) 19 of 126 onions did, and the same onion in 4 shots of one pile scored anywhere from 0.2 to 0.8. unhealthy_at (0.5) only decides which way the grade leans.
